basics.label: The point
basics.title: Catch it in the end zone
basics.text: Seven a side. You score by catching a pass inside the end zone you're attacking. First to 15 wins, half time at 8.

basics.label: The catch
basics.title: You can't run with it
basics.text: Once you catch the disc you stop and plant a pivot foot. The other foot goes anywhere. Throw in any direction — forwards, sideways, backwards.

basics.label: The clock
basics.title: Ten seconds to throw
basics.text: The defender guarding you counts out loud, one number per second. If they start saying "ten" before you release, it's a turnover.

basics.label: The flip
basics.title: Drop it and it's theirs
basics.text: Incomplete pass, interception, or out-of-bounds — possession flips instantly, right where it happened. No whistle, no reset. Turn and defend.

basics.label: The contact
basics.title: It's a non-contact sport
basics.text: You must try to avoid initiating contact, and "I was going for the disc" is explicitly not an excuse. Minor brushes aren't fouls.

basics.label: The difference
basics.title: Nobody is refereeing
basics.text: Players make every call themselves, including against themselves. Disagree? Say "contest", talk it out, and the disc goes back to the thrower.

situations.q: I caught it. How long do I have to throw?
situations.a: Ten seconds, counted out loud by your marker at no faster than one number per second. It's a turnover only once they start to say "ten" — and only if a defender is actually counting. If nobody is within three metres of you calling numbers, there is no clock at all.

situations.q: The disc hit the ground. What now?
situations.a: Instant turnover, no stoppage. The other team picks it up where it stopped and attacks the other way. Nobody checks it in, nobody resets — so if you were on offence, turn around and guard someone immediately.

situations.q: I caught it in the end zone but landed on the line. Is that a goal?
situations.a: No. The goal line belongs to the central zone, so all of your ground contact has to be entirely past it. You haven't lost the disc though — walk to the nearest point on the goal line and set your pivot there.

situations.q: I stepped on the sideline. Am I out?
situations.a: Yes. Unusually for a field sport, the perimeter lines are not part of the playing field. Touching the sideline while you contact the disc means it's a turnover and no catch is deemed to have happened.

situations.q: Someone called "travel" on me. Do we stop?
situations.a: No. Travel is an infraction, so play continues. You move back to the correct pivot spot — the caller shows you where — and while you do, the stall count is paused and you may not throw. Then the count resumes.

situations.q: Can I call a foul for my team-mate?
situations.a: No. Only the player who was fouled may call a foul. You can absolutely offer what you saw during the discussion — perspective from a player with a good view is valuable and encouraged.

situations.q: We disagree and neither of us will budge. Who wins?
situations.a: Nobody. The disc goes back to the last undisputed thrower and play restarts with a check. That's the designed outcome for genuine disagreement — it's not a failure, it's the system working.

situations.q: The marker is counting way too fast. What do I say?
situations.a: Call "fast count". Play doesn't stop; the marker resets to the correct number and carries on. If they keep doing it, you can escalate to a marking violation, which does stop play.

situations.q: Two defenders are on me. Is that allowed?
situations.a: Only if the second one is genuinely guarding another offensive player. A defender within three metres of your pivot who isn't guarding anyone is a double team — and unusually, any offensive player can make this call, not just you.

situations.q: Someone called a foul while the disc was in the air. Do I stop running?
situations.a: No — finish the play. Play continues until someone catches it or it lands. If the team that made the call ends up with the disc, the play just stands. Only then do you sort out what happens.

situations.q: Play stopped. Where am I supposed to stand?
situations.a: Exactly where you were when the call was made, and stay still until the disc is checked in. Drifting to a better position during a stoppage is itself a violation, and the other team can call it after the check.

situations.q: How do we actually restart after a stoppage?
situations.a: If a defender is within reach of the thrower, they touch the disc. If not, the thrower touches the disc to the ground and calls "Disc In". Both sides check their own team-mates are ready first.

situations.q: The pull went straight out of bounds. Where do we start?
situations.a: Your choice: the brick mark — the cross in the middle of the field, one end-zone-length in from your goal line — or the spot where it crossed the sideline. Signal the brick with a raised arm before you pick the disc up.

situations.q: I'm brand new and I don't know a rule. What do I do?
situations.a: Say so. The rules explicitly tell experienced players to explain breaches to novices rather than take advantage, and allow an experienced player to supervise beginner games. "I'm new — can you explain that?" is a completely normal sentence on an ultimate field.

situations.q: Can I go out of bounds to catch it?
situations.a: You can run out there, but where you touch the disc is what counts. Any part of you out-of-bounds when you contact the disc is a turnover. Catch it airborne and land in-bounds first, and you're fine — even if momentum carries you out afterwards.

situations.q: I got tangled up chasing my player. Can I do anything?
situations.a: Call "Pick" — but only if being obstructed actually stopped you moving with the player you were guarding. You may wait up to two seconds to see if it mattered. Play stops and you move to where you would have got to.

The next point starts immediately, teams switch which end zone they're defending, and the team that just scored pulls. Substitute freely in that window — but once your team signals ready for the pull, the line is set.

situations.q: How many time-outs do we get?
situations.a: The core rules don't say — it's set by your event or league format, so ask your captain. What the rules do say: after the pull only a thrower holding the disc can call one, it lasts 75 seconds, and the stall count restarts at maximum nine.
